children: Prof Dr M Srinivas calls for common minimum standards for patient safety and quality across hospitals, alongside greater access to affordable healthcare in smaller cities

The Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM) could transform healthcare delivery in India and other countries across the Global South by enabling the use of structured, interoperable health data for artificial intelligence (AI), Prof Dr M Srinivas, Member of NITI Aayog, said on Tuesday.

Addressing the 20th edition of FICCI HEAL 2026 in New Delhi on 27 October, Srinivas said India had established a digital health ecosystem through ABDM and was working towards a common platform connecting Ayushman Bharat Health Account (ABHA) IDs with electronic health records.

“Data is a goldmine for us. Once this data is harnessed, AI can be optimally utilized, allowing us to achieve transformative outcomes not only for the nation but also for the Global South,” he said. Srinivas said the National Health Authority was working to establish structured health data with interoperability, with the aim of enabling electronic health records to operate across a common digital platform.

Alongside digital health infrastructure, Srinivas called for hospitals to establish minimum standards for patient safety and quality of care. He said both government and private hospitals needed to meet a basic standard that would allow India’s healthcare system to gain global recognition for the quality of patient care. “The country should have a basic minimum standard of quality and safety at every hospital. As a country, we must come to a level where the world should recognize that Indian hospitals have a minimum standard of patient care,” he said.

He also stressed the need to place patients at the centre of healthcare delivery by ensuring timely treatment and protecting households from additional financial burdens. He cited the Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY) as a key focus in this regard. Srinivas said the rising burden of non-communicable diseases required greater attention to prevention rather than an approach centred primarily on treatment at tertiary-care hospitals.

Srinivas said hospitals needed to combine clinical care with a stronger focus on the patient experience. He called on private hospitals to extend affordable healthcare services to tier-2 and tier-3 cities to address the unequal distribution of healthcare facilities.

He also urged private hospitals to adopt universal health coverage schemes, emphasising the need to improve affordability and access alongside patient safety and quality standards. The comments come as healthcare stakeholders discuss the sector’s role in achieving the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047, with investment, preventive care, workforce development and public-private collaboration emerging as key priorities at the conference.
Industry Calls For Greater Access And Innovation

Dr Kenji Shibuya, CEO of Medical Excellence JAPAN, said India and Japan had an opportunity to work together on healthcare transformation. He highlighted India’s Heal in India initiative and its combination of advanced medical care, Ayurveda and wellness services as part of its ambition to become a global healthcare destination.

Dr Ashutosh Raghuvanshi, Chair of the FICCI Health Services Committee and Managing Director and CEO of Fortis Healthcare, said the healthcare sector needed to combine world-class capabilities with affordability, access and trust to support the Viksit Bharat 2047 vision. He identified sustained investment, stronger prevention and early diagnosis, a skilled healthcare workforce, and closer collaboration between the public and private sectors as requirements for achieving that objective.

Anuj Pasrija, Country Lead, J&J MedTech India, and Vice President-Surgery at Johnson & Johnson, said future hospitals would need to maintain continuity of care beyond their physical infrastructure. “The hospital of the future will not be defined merely by its buildings, beds, or operating rooms. It will be defined by its ability to stay connected with the patient across the entire journey of patient care,” he said.

Varun Khanna, Co-Chair of the FICCI Health Services Committee and Managing Director and Group CEO of Aster DM Quality Care, called for a healthcare system that prioritises accessibility, affordability, equity, innovation and quality. The 20th edition of FICCI HEAL, held under the theme ‘HEAL@20: From Vision to Value’, brought together healthcare stakeholders to discuss the sector’s priorities and its contribution to India’s long-term development goals.
